scope: Focused correctness and dependency recheck of proposed 04b timing repair, prior Brownian teaching and glossary, unchanged Part2 purpose and global description. No Stage2 wording or Stage3 flow acceptance.

resolved.quote: The integral against dW(u) denotes the limit of these weighted sums as h tends to zero.
resolved.judgment: The reader now has an operation they can construct from the previously taught independent Brownian increments. The same-increment variance h and vanishing distinct-increment products explicitly justify replacing the covariance sum by the ordinary exponential overlap integral. This supplies the missing reasoning rather than only naming stochastic integration.

passage_judgments.quote: It starts at zero, has continuous paths and independent Gaussian increments with mean zero
passage_judgments.reason: These properties are stated before θ=θ0+√(2D)W and MSD=2Dt. The earlier finite-step assumptions supply the scale 2Ddt; mean zero distinguishes variance from uncentered MSD, and continuity distinguishes Brownian paths from jump processes. No equation changed and the ensuing bias example still has both contributions v²t²+2Dt.

passage_judgments.quote: The bracketed increment is independent of W(s) and has mean zero
passage_judgments.reason: Min(s,t) covariance still follows from the newly explicit assumptions. The local/unbounded qualification remains after the covariance derivation and before later eye use.

passage_judgments.quote: independent Gaussian increments of mean zero and variance equal to elapsed time
passage_judgments.reason: Matches the main-text Brownian definition and the later increment mean/variance used in the weighted-sum covariance. Glossary supplements actual earlier teaching rather than supplying the dependency alone.

passage_judgments.quote: Define velocity v=dot E=(B-E)/τ. Taking its increment gives τdv=-vdt+√(2D)dW.
passage_judgments.reason: Low-pass/white-noise/covariance stationarity and Brownian coefficient are taught before the repair. Differentiating B-E by increments uses dE=vdt, giving a negative velocity-restoring term and positive random input. With τ>0, the exponential attenuation is stable.

passage_judgments.quote: Its contribution to the velocity at time t is approximately (√(2D)/τ)e^{-(t-u_j)/τ}ΔW_j
passage_judgments.reason: For past times u_j≤t the age t-u_j is nonnegative, so the factor decays as required. Using the start of a short interval is an approximation whose difference vanishes as h→0. ΔW has mean0, varianceh and independent disjoint increments, all supplied by earlier Brownian teaching. √(2D)/τ has units deg/s^(3/2), while ΔW has units s^(1/2), giving velocity deg/s. This is enough for the deterministic-weight integral used here; no state-dependent integration rule is needed.

passage_judgments.quote: After the initial velocity has decayed, extending the input history into the distant past gives
passage_judgments.reason: This preserves the stationary-velocity idealization. It denotes the limiting long-running stable filter after the finite-start initial term has decayed; it does not assert that Brownian position has stationary variance. A finite starting time t0 would give e^{-(t-t0)/τ}v(t0) plus an integral from t0 to t. Taking the distant-past limit removes that term and makes the stated covariance independent of t. The passage explicitly presents this history extension, so a separate lesson on two-sided Brownian construction is unnecessary for the calculation.

passage_judgments.quote: The same increment contributes its variance h
passage_judgments.reason: Zero mean makes distinct independent increment products vanish. Shared history stops at t for s≥0, and the product weights are exp[-(t-u)/τ]exp[-(t+s-u)/τ]. Setting r=t-u reverses the integration endpoints, producing an ordinary positive integral from0 to∞; its value is τ/2. Thus (2D/τ²)e^{-s/τ}(τ/2)=D/τ e^{-s/τ}. Velocity mean0 makes this covariance equal to the raw product expectation. C_v has units deg²/s². Symmetry in positive/negative lag follows because this is the covariance of one stationary real-valued velocity.

The repair connects directly to the unchanged position-displacement double covariance integral. Integrating the positive even exponential covariance gives the displayed MSD, its short-lag (D/τ)ℓ² and long-lag2D(ℓ-τ) limits. The local-slope values and guide-model qualification remain valid. The repair adds no input that changes the earlier amplitude-normalization or full-muscle-model comparison.

passage_judgments.quote: Neural fluctuations reach behavior through a motor pathway, while spatial tuning describes how a position is expressed across cells.
passage_judgments.reason: Part2 purpose agrees with the eye sequence and the frontmatter's separate statistical map study. It does not claim that observed place-field statistics provide a dynamical noise law or that χ uniquely identifies integrator neurons.

passage_judgments.quote: This guide teaches the neural background and central derivations
passage_judgments.reason: Description matches the selected three papers and explicit reading-path orientation. The repaired weighted Brownian derivation remains a clearly labeled guide teaching reconstruction rather than falsely attributed original-paper algebra.
